reason: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and every reference, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms for ask --wait, the send delivery-wait rename and the deprecation of send --reply, rebased onto public main's true-today guidance. Where the Agent Session has a proven return path (Claude Code, Codex, Grok, the Hermes classic CLI, OpenClaw on macOS), ask --wait registers the question at once and exits 0 with next.end_turn true; its output says to ask it in the conversation, say what each answer will make you do, then end the turn, and the answer arrives as the next message. A repeated ask --wait re-attaches to the open question; it never takes the Codex card; a hooked session whose routing is not ready is refused as plain ask is. Where no later answer can reach the Agent Session (no harness, conflicting markers, Cursor, OpenCode, OpenClaw off macOS, Hermes off its classic CLI), plain ask still refuses with the shipped code for that case (session_identity_missing, session_identity_ambiguous or question_routing_unavailable), now with a remedy naming notifai ask --wait (in OpenCode also its question form or the conversation), and ask --wait holds the command: for the harness command limit minus 10 s (Claude Code 110 s or BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS minus 10 s, Cursor 590 s, anything unmeasured 110 s), or for reply_window_seconds with no harness; no flag sets it. A held wait submits at once and skips the terminal-first delay. The service ends the question at that deadline; SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP withdraw it. Exit 0 prints the answer, and a program with no harness records the receipt "Received by the program that asked."; exit 3 says the question ended unanswered and is off the User's devices; exit 5 says an answer may be waiting until the deadline and names notifai replies. A disabled Project refuses ask --wait with project_disabled and questions off with question_routing_disabled, as for ask. Guidance: main taught send --reply wherever no answer can return, so this change makes the guidance true for ask --wait. The skill's Ask section says to keep working with notifai ask or stop with notifai ask --wait and end the turn, and that a wait held in the command can end unanswered (exit 3); the Bounded foreground wait section is gone; the trust-gap line says do not work around it; questions off says ask --wait refuses too; exit rows 3 and 5 describe ask --wait. Harness setup names notifai ask --wait where no answer can come back and for conflicting markers, with no command timeout shorter than the harness default. The Cursor, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes references name ask --wait in place of send --reply; Grok's says to end the turn after ask --wait; Codex's says ask --wait never opens a card; Claude Code's says ask --wait tells the agent to end its turn. The Cursor, OpenCode, OpenClaw-off-macOS and Hermes delivery contracts, the Cursor Stop note, the exact-session diagnostic, the Codex hook-trust refusal ("Neither notifai ask nor notifai ask --wait works until the User approves the hooks") and the ask_grace_seconds and reply_window_seconds explanations say the same. send help names --delivery-timeout <seconds>; send --wait, --no-wait, --reply and its flags, and replies --wait stay accepted, hidden, each with one deprecation line. No readiness id, hook definition or protocol field changed. Earlier, kept: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and every reference, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms for text and number pickers. A Claude Code host that turns on the extended question schema can open a picker whose questions ask for typed text or a number; plain terminal claude still sends only choices. A self-opened picker with such questions now reaches the User's devices as free-text questions: a number question's Body states its range ("A number from 5 to 20 slides, in steps of 5."), each question's helper line goes into the Body under it, its heading becomes the title, option previews stay in the terminal, and the picker still links. A device answer returns as the picker's own typed value, and a terminal answer is recorded as text. So the Claude Code reference's "a picker you open on your own is the Notifai question too", "its heading, or else its headers, becomes the title" and "typed text can stand beside or instead of a choice" are true for every shape Claude Code offers, and it already names no picker shape as terminal-only. A picker question kind Notifai does not know stays in the terminal with reason unsupported-question-kind. No guidance wording, command, flag, readiness id, hook definition or protocol field changed. Earlier, kept: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and every reference, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms for the Claude Code picker core. Questions: ask registers a closed-choice question on Claude Code instead of refusing it into the picker (the use_question_picker refusal is gone, which no agent had to handle as success), and the duplicate guard registers one question whichever route came first, so "never also ask it" and "never register an open question again" stay true; a repeated ask exits 0 with registered: false and already_open and applies no new Body or images. Titles: the skill's ask example passes --title and says to write it as the titles topic says for a question; the titles topic says a question's title names the decision and a form's title everything it decides; the form format and the worked question example carry titles. A title an older skill or script leaves out is a one-line stderr note, not a usage error: the question is titled by the Agent Session name, the rule self-opened forms follow, and an untitled question of several shows as "Question N"; ask --help says always pass --title. A self-opened picker is titled by its heading, else its headers, else the Agent Session name; a Codex card by the Agent Session name; the CLI never copies the question into the title. Picker results: a picker Claude Code continued while the User was away is not an answer and its question stays open, with context saying the answer arrives as the next message; typed text is recorded as the terminal answer; a request for another round, Esc, "Chat about this" and a denial withdraw the device question, settled by the picker's result within a 5 s bound; the context for a device answer beside a terminal answer names both without calling both the User's own. No readiness id, hook definition or protocol field changed.
